stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Finite locally free morphisms are affine and have a finite locally free pushforward of the structure sheaf.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a representable morphism
of algebraic spaces over $S$. Then $f$ is finite locally free
(in the sense of Section \ref{section-representable})
if and only if $f$ is affine and the sheaf $f_*\mathcal{O}_X$ is
a finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a representable morphism
of algebraic spaces over $S$.
conclusions:
$f$ is finite locally free
(in the sense of Section \ref{section-representable})
if and only if $f$ is affine and the sheaf $f_*\mathcal{O}_X$ is
a finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module.

reason: If f is finite locally free, its structure-sheaf pushforward becomes finite locally free after a surjective étale chart; descent makes the pushforward finite locally free. Conversely an affine map with finite locally free pushforward is locally finite locally free on charts, and the descent theorem recovers f finite locally free.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Finite locally free morphisms are affine and have a finite locally free pushforward of the structure sheaf.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is representable and finite locally free,
\item $f$ is finite locally free,
\item there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is finite locally free, and
\item there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each morphism $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is finite locally free.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
conclusions: $f$ is representable and finite locally free,

there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is finite locally free, and

there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each morphism $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is finite locally free.

reason: A surjective étale chart with finite locally free base-change yields a scheme affine over the chart, and effective descent of finite locally free morphisms gives global representability and the property. It is local in the Zariski and fpqc topology, yielding all four equivalences.
